exercise.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Calf Raise
library_steps: Stand on one leg on a step, holding a dumbbell on that side.
Hold a rail with your free hand for balance.
Let your heel drop, then rise onto your toes as high as you can.
Lower slowly, then switch sides after your set.
exercise.one_line_summary: On the ball of the left foot at the edge of a 15 cm step, knee straight, dumbbell in the left hand, right hand on a wall: heel dropped below the step (start), then up high on the toes (end).

setup.target: Ball of the foot firmly on the step edge, heel hanging off.
setup.tolerance: ball 2-4 cm in from the edge

setup.target: Free hand on a wall or rail for balance only; free leg bent behind.

movement.measure: foot pitch vs flat, + = heel up (spec foot rot X)
ankle centre z (m), ball fixed at step top 0.15
rises straight up with the ankle, no hip bend

muscles.role: Lift the heel. Straight knee keeps the gastrocnemius (the main calf muscle) working.
Keeps the pelvis level on one leg.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Knee bends and the hip drops as the heel lowers.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Turns it into a dip; less calf range.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Heel never goes below the step or never rises high.
mistakes.why_it_matters: The step is there for the full stretch and full rise.

sources.citation: American Council on Exercise. Standing Calf Raises - Wall (exercise library).
sources.what_it_gave: Hands on the wall, knees straight, feet not rotated; single-leg variation lifts one foot; targets gastrocnemius.

sources.citation: Jo S. 2015. Get stronger calves with these 5 exercises. ACE expert articles.
sources.what_it_gave: Single-leg heel raise on a step: ball of foot on the step, heel below the edge, rise as high as possible, knee straight, 10-15 reps.
